one_line_idea: Entropy-minimization test-time adaptation gains are specialized to synthetic corruption-style shifts and vanish or reverse on natural distribution shifts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The unlabeled-adaptation signal exploited by entropy minimization is only reliable when the shift preserves class-conditional structure the way synthetic corruptions do, so gains fail to transfer to natural shifts such as geographic, temporal, or population change.

one_line_idea: Test-time adaptation hyperparameters are implicitly tuned on the test distribution, making reported gains circular; shift-blind hyperparameter selection erases most of them.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The published hyperparameters encode oracle knowledge of the test shift, and under a rigorous protocol where hyperparameters must be fixed before seeing the shift, most methods lose most of their advantage over the unadapted baseline.

one_line_idea: Core test-time adaptation conclusions were formed on batch-normalized convolutional networks and do not transfer to layer-normalized transformer foundation models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The mechanism, stability properties, and method rankings of test-time adaptation change qualitatively when the backbone is a layer-normalized transformer, so a substantial portion of accepted best practice is architecture-era-specific rather than general.

one_line_idea: Under long unlabeled streams, most self-supervised test-time adaptation methods eventually collapse to trivial predictions, and collapse frequency is a hidden but decisive metric.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Collapse is not an edge case but the asymptotic behavior of most unsupervised adaptation objectives, so extending evaluation horizon by one to two orders of magnitude will reveal widespread collapse that current protocols never measure.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-A-091 (self-training/TTA degeneracy; G-005 generalizes the collapse phenomenon to long unlabeled streams with collapse frequency as the metric)

one_line_idea: A frozen foundation model with a test-time nearest-neighbor or retrieval-augmented classifier matches gradient-based test-time adaptation at far lower risk.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Accumulating test embeddings in a memory and classifying by neighborhood vote or prototype update captures most of the benefit that parameter-updating adaptation achieves, because the useful adaptation signal is a shift in feature-space class geometry rather than in the features themselves.

one_line_idea: Most of what test-time adaptation improves is calibration and decision thresholds, not representation quality, and a post-hoc output correction recovers the bulk of its accuracy gain.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant effect of popular adaptation methods is equivalent to a shift-conditional rescaling and re-prioring of the output distribution, so a purely post-hoc correction that estimates test-class marginals and temperature achieves most of the same accuracy gain without touching features.

flags: banned_cluster_adjacent:calibration/uncertainty (capped master family): TTA-gain attribution to calibration; subject is TTA, watch the family count

one_line_idea: Test-time adaptation methods are doing implicit label-shift estimation, and explicit unlabeled class-prior correction matches them whenever the shift includes a prior change.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A significant fraction of test-time adaptation benefit on realistic shifts is attributable to implicit prior correction, so on shifts constructed to have pure prior change, explicit classical estimators will match or beat gradient-based adaptation.

one_line_idea: Single-sample adaptation methods built on augmentation consistency mostly repackage test-time augmentation ensembling, and the learning component adds little.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The augmentation-averaged prediction alone, with no parameter update, captures the majority of the reported gain, so the gradient step contributes a minor and sometimes negative residual.

one_line_idea: No current test-time adaptation method knows when not to adapt; a simple do-no-harm gate based on stream statistics prevents most catastrophic adaptation failures.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A lightweight gate that monitors cheap statistics, such as embedding-distribution distance from a pretraining reference and prediction-marginal skew, can decide when to enable adaptation and thereby eliminate the majority of negative-gain episodes while retaining most positive-gain episodes.

one_line_idea: Periodic hard reset to source weights beats sophisticated anti-forgetting machinery in continual test-time adaptation over long horizons.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The entire benefit of these mechanisms is approximated by periodically resetting all adapted parameters to the source checkpoint, because the useful adaptation state is cheap to reacquire while accumulated drift is expensive to undo.

one_line_idea: Episodic reset-per-shift evaluation protocols overstate test-time adaptation practicality, and realistic recurring mixed-shift streams reverse published method rankings.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Method rankings are protocol-dependent, and under unannounced recurring mixed shifts, methods that look strong episodically will underperform simpler or memory-based approaches because their state management assumptions break.

one_line_idea: Matching test images to the pretraining input-statistics envelope, a trivial input-space normalization, is a stronger and safer baseline than most parameter-updating test-time adaptation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Estimating simple global statistics of the test stream and transforming inputs toward the pretraining envelope recovers a large share of shift-induced degradation on low-level shifts, matching parameter-updating methods there while being trivially reversible.

one_line_idea: Classical unsupervised domain adaptation methods built for weak backbones add approximately nothing on top of modern foundation-model features.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The gap those methods closed was a feature-quality gap, not a fundamental adaptation gap, so with a frozen strong foundation backbone plus simple target-side self-training, adversarial alignment and discrepancy-minimization methods provide no additional benefit.

one_line_idea: Marginal feature-alignment objectives actively hurt adaptation when source and target label distributions differ, and popular benchmarks hide this by having nearly matched label marginals.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Standard benchmark pairs have incidentally similar label marginals, which is why the harm is invisible; introducing controlled label-proportion mismatch will make alignment methods underperform source-only baselines with a severity that grows with the mismatch.

one_line_idea: Zero-shot vision-language models have effectively saturated office-style adaptation benchmarks, making continued method development on them uninformative.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On these benchmarks, zero-shot performance of public vision-language models is within a small margin of the best published adaptation results that use unlabeled target data, implying the benchmarks no longer measure adaptation ability.

one_line_idea: Unsupervised model selection, not adaptation method choice, is the dominant source of variance in domain adaptation outcomes, and reported method gains are smaller than selection-induced spread.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The spread of target accuracy across defensible unsupervised selection criteria applied to one method's training run exceeds the typical published gap between competing methods, meaning the literature's method rankings are inside the selection noise band.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-079 / W13-P1-C-047 (selection- and variance-dominance templates; G-019's unsupervised-model-selection instrument is subject-native)

one_line_idea: Source data hurts more than it helps once a strong foundation initialization exists: source-free adaptation matches or beats joint source-plus-target training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] With a foundation-model initialization, continued training on source data anchors the model to source-specific decision structure, so removing source data during adaptation is neutral or beneficial rather than a handicap.

one_line_idea: A cheap a-priori adaptability score computed from foundation-model feature geometry predicts whether unsupervised adaptation will help, do nothing, or hurt on a given domain pair.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Simple statistics of source and target embeddings under a frozen foundation model, such as class-cluster overlap and marginal distance decomposed into class-relevant and class-irrelevant directions, carry enough signal to predict the sign and rough magnitude of adaptation gain before any adaptation runs.

one_line_idea: Domain invariance is the wrong objective: methods that succeed do so through implicit class-conditional alignment, and enforcing pure marginal invariance strictly removes target-discriminative information.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Successful runs of invariance-based methods achieve their gains during phases where the learned representation is not actually domain-invariant but conditionally aligned given predicted class, so measured invariance will anti-correlate with target accuracy within training trajectories.

one_line_idea: In dense-prediction domain adaptation, a large share of reported gains comes from resolution, crop, and class-frequency handling rather than from distribution-alignment machinery.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Applying only the input-pipeline and sampling engineering of leading segmentation-adaptation methods, with no adaptation objective at all, recovers a majority of their reported gain over naive source training.

one_line_idea: Adaptation methods developed on synthetic-to-real style gaps systematically fail on real-to-real shifts such as geography and time, because the two gap types have different structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Methods tuned for rendering-gap transfer exploit low-level regularities absent in real-to-real shifts, so their ranking and even their sign of benefit fail to transfer from the synthetic-to-real regime to real-to-real regimes.

one_line_idea: Domain-generalization benchmarks primarily rank pretrained backbones rather than generalization algorithms, and published algorithm rankings are noise around a backbone-determined score.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A variance decomposition over the published literature and controlled reruns will attribute the large majority of score variance to backbone and selection protocol, with algorithm identity explaining a small residual that fails to replicate across reruns.

one_line_idea: Invariance-penalty methods fail on vision benchmarks because the annotated environments are not causally meaningful, and with environments constructed from capture metadata the same methods start working.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The reported failure of invariance penalties is an environment-quality failure rather than a theory failure, so re-partitioning existing data into environments aligned with plausible nuisance factors, such as capture hardware or acquisition context, will recover measurable invariance-penalty gains over plain training.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Constructive rescue inside a debunk shard: invariance methods fail because annotated environments are not causally meaningful, and metadata-built environments revive them. Tension partner of G-026.

one_line_idea: Weight-averaging and flat-minima methods improve domain-generalization scores through generic variance reduction that helps in-distribution equally, not through any shift-specific mechanism.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The improvement is a uniform accuracy lift from implicit ensembling that applies identically to in-distribution test data, so the ratio of out-of-distribution to in-distribution gain will be near one, contradicting shift-specific explanations.

one_line_idea: Pretraining data diversity, not model scale, is the dominant controllable factor for out-of-domain generalization at fixed compute.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At fixed compute and fixed data quantity, increasing the diversity of pretraining data sources yields larger out-of-domain gains than increasing model size, and diversity effects dominate the out-of-domain scaling curve.

one_line_idea: Per unit of in-distribution accuracy, frozen-feature linear probes generalize across domains better than end-to-end fine-tuned models, and the gap widens with shift severity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The probing-versus-fine-tuning robustness tradeoff is systematic and monotone in shift severity, so an accuracy-matched comparison across many shift levels will show probes dominating fine-tuned models out-of-distribution at every matched in-distribution accuracy level.

one_line_idea: Compositional shift, where familiar attributes and objects appear in novel combinations, is a distinct failure axis of vision foundation models that standard domain-generalization metrics never measure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation models degrade sharply and systematically on held-out combinations even when every constituent factor is well represented in training, and this degradation is uncorrelated with their scores on standard shift benchmarks.

one_line_idea: Leave-one-domain-out evaluation has such high variance across the choice of held-out domain that most published domain-generalization comparisons are statistically undecidable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The distribution over held-out-domain results is so heavy-tailed and method-domain interaction so strong that the averaged score has confidence intervals wider than typical reported method gaps, rendering most pairwise method comparisons undecidable at benchmark scale.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-047 (evaluation-design variance exceeds method gaps; LODO-variance instrument is subject-native)

one_line_idea: Frozen foundation-model embeddings with classical two-sample tests detect deployment distribution shift better than dedicated learned shift detectors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The detection problem becomes easy in a good representation, so a frozen general-purpose embedding combined with classical multivariate two-sample statistics matches or beats specialized detectors across realistic shift types at a fraction of the operational cost.

one_line_idea: Most distribution shifts flagged by monitoring systems do not harm accuracy, and harm-calibrated detection, not shift detection, is the correct monitoring objective.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In realistic deployment streams the majority of statistically detectable shifts are accuracy-neutral, so detectors optimized for distributional sensitivity have precision far below what harm-targeted detectors achieve at equal recall of genuinely harmful shifts.

one_line_idea: Unlabeled accuracy-estimation methods fail precisely on the shift types where monitoring needs them most, and a failure taxonomy predicts when their estimates can be trusted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] These estimators share an assumption that confidence remains informative of correctness under the shift, which holds for low-level covariate shifts but fails under semantic, label-prior, and spurious-correlation shifts, producing confidently wrong accuracy estimates exactly when the model is most degraded.

one_line_idea: The accuracy-on-the-line phenomenon is a property of shared pretraining lineages, and it breaks for adapted, fine-tuned, or intervention-modified models, undermining its use for monitoring.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The linear trend is generated by models sharing pretraining data and training recipes, so models modified by test-time adaptation, robust fine-tuning, or targeted interventions will fall systematically off the line, making line-based prediction unreliable exactly for the models robustness research produces.

one_line_idea: Embedding-space shift detection is dominated by low-level image statistics, masking semantic shifts; band-separated tests are needed to see what actually changed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Standard embedding statistics respond much more strongly to low-level factors than to semantic factors of equal harm, so a semantic shift co-occurring with a mild low-level change is detected as the low-level change and its semantic component goes unnoticed.

one_line_idea: Anytime-valid sequential tests on foundation-model embeddings give deployment shift alarms with controlled false-alarm rates, which matters more in practice than the detection-power race.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Martingale-based and conformal sequential tests over frozen embeddings provide practically sufficient detection latency while guaranteeing false-alarm control under continuous monitoring, and the lack of such control, not lack of power, is why practitioners distrust current detectors.

flags: banned_cluster_adjacent:calibration/uncertainty (capped master family): sequential-testing false-alarm control instrument

one_line_idea: Predicting per-sample correctness under shift is more tractable than predicting aggregate accuracy, and selective prediction transfers across shifts better than accuracy estimation does.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The per-sample question, whether this prediction is trustworthy, retains usable signal under shifts that break aggregate estimation, because instance-level features of failure generalize while population-level confidence calibration does not.

one_line_idea: Rankings from out-of-distribution detection benchmarks do not predict which methods detect harmful natural shift in deployment-like monitoring, revealing a benchmark-objective mismatch.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The suite task, distinguishing wholly different datasets, rewards features irrelevant to detecting gradual harmful drift within a deployment distribution, so method rankings on the suites will correlate poorly with rankings on realistic drift-monitoring tasks.

one_line_idea: Label-shift estimators silently return confident nonsense when class-conditional distributions also shift, and a cheap self-diagnostic can flag when their assumption is violated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Realistic shifts almost always violate the conditional-invariance assumption to some degree, causing prior estimates with large errors that carry no warning sign, but internal consistency statistics of the estimator, such as confusion-matrix compatibility across data splits, can detect the violation without labels.

one_line_idea: Drift root-cause attribution, assigning a detected shift to interpretable factors via counterfactual reweighting in foundation-feature space, is more valuable and more tractable than drift detection itself.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reweighting reference data to match the shifted stream within interpretable factor subspaces of a foundation embedding, and measuring how much each factor's reweighting explains the detected divergence, produces attribution that agrees with ground-truth causes in controlled scenarios.

one_line_idea: Hidden batch effects inside single-domain vision test sets shrink effective sample size so much that standard error bars in evaluation papers are systematically overconfident.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cluster structure in standard test sets reduces effective sample size by a large factor for typical accuracy comparisons, so many published significant differences between models would not survive cluster-aware inference.

one_line_idea: Data augmentation is an unacknowledged train-time distribution shift, and its interaction with test-time shift explains part of why augmentation-trained models respond unpredictably to deployment drift.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The augmentation policy defines a reference envelope, and a model's response to a test-time shift depends primarily on whether the shift lies inside or outside that envelope, making the augmentation policy, not the raw data, the correct object for predicting shift response.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Reframes augmentation as an unacknowledged train-time distribution shift interacting with test-time shift — a mechanism nobody in the shard's eval-critique mass touches.

one_line_idea: Dataset curation filters make benchmark test sets systematically easier than deployment data, and the curation-induced optimism is quantifiable by reconstructing the rejected data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The accuracy gap between curated test sets and uncurated streams from the same nominal distribution is large, model-dependent, and dominated by the curation filters themselves, so re-collecting data with filters removed provides a direct measurement of curation optimism.

one_line_idea: Deployed vision models reshape the future data they receive, and this feedback loop breaks i.i.d. evaluation in a way measurable only through simulation-based protocols.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under realistic feedback dynamics, model performance trajectories diverge substantially from what any static test set predicts, with error concentrating in regions the model's own decisions made rare in its observable stream, and simulation of the loop is sufficient to expose the divergence.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Performativity: deployed models reshape their own future data, breaking i.i.d. evaluation in a way only simulation protocols can measure. No template family; protect.

one_line_idea: Shuffling time-stamped datasets hides temporal drift; time-respecting splits materially change both absolute accuracy and model rankings on the same data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training on early data and testing on late data from the same dataset will reveal consistent accuracy drops and ranking changes relative to shuffled splits, demonstrating that conventional splits overstate deployment performance even with zero nominal domain change.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-029 (benchmark aging; G-051's time-respecting-split protocol is a distinct instrument)

one_line_idea: Realistic dependence structure in deployment streams breaks conformal prediction coverage for vision models, and the realized coverage gap is large enough to matter operationally.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under realistic vision-stream dependence, realized coverage of standard conformal methods deviates from nominal by operationally meaningful margins in stretches that matter, such as during bursts, even when long-run average coverage looks acceptable.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-015 (conformal failures under shift; G-053's mechanism is dependence/non-exchangeability, not covariate shift)
banned_cluster_adjacent:calibration/uncertainty (capped master family): conformal coverage member; master C-015 adjacent

one_line_idea: Foundation-model robustness gains on shift benchmarks are largely pretraining-coverage effects, and an explicit coverage audit deflates claimed robustness to genuine novelty.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For most celebrated foundation-model robustness results, the shifted test distribution is well covered by pretraining data, and robustness measured against coverage-controlled shift strata will show ordinary, unremarkable degradation, reducing claimed robustness to a data-coverage bookkeeping fact.

one_line_idea: A time-travel evaluation using only imagery created after a model's data cutoff provides the first clean measurement of foundation-model robustness to genuine novelty.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Robustness measured on post-cutoff imagery, including new products, events, aesthetics, and camera pipelines, will be systematically lower than robustness measured on standard benchmarks for the same models, and the gap will grow with time since cutoff.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Time-travel evaluation on post-cutoff imagery as the only clean novelty-robustness measurement. Instrument-defining; protect from coverage-family consolidation (it is the family's decisive test).

one_line_idea: Robustness loss under downstream fine-tuning is a smooth function of parameter movement from the pretrained point, giving a practical dial for the accuracy-robustness tradeoff.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Effective robustness declines monotonically and smoothly with a measure of parameter displacement from the pretrained checkpoint, approximately independent of which fine-tuning method produced the displacement, making displacement a sufficient statistic for robustness loss.

one_line_idea: Out-of-distribution performance saturates with model scale earlier than in-distribution performance, indicating that robustness is data-limited rather than capacity-limited.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At fixed pretraining data, out-of-distribution accuracy as a function of model size flattens earlier than in-distribution accuracy, so beyond a modest scale, additional parameters buy in-distribution polish but no robustness, and only data changes move the out-of-distribution ceiling.

one_line_idea: Foundation models are relatively less robust to low-level sensor and compression shifts than smaller supervised models, and their celebrated robustness advantage is semantic-only.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Web-scale pretraining concentrates diversity in semantics and style but is homogeneous in imaging pipeline statistics, so foundation models will show robustness advantages on semantic shifts and reduced or reversed advantages on low-level imaging shifts relative to supervised baselines trained with heavy low-level augmentation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Contrarian sign-flip: foundation models LESS robust than small supervised models on low-level sensor/compression shifts — attacks the shard's own robustness-optimism and the field's.

one_line_idea: Measured robustness differences between zero-shot and probed versions of the same backbone show that the classification head, not the representation, drives much of the foundation-model robustness story.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The text-derived head encodes class structure independent of any downstream dataset's statistics while the probe head absorbs source-dataset biases, so a large share of the zero-shot robustness advantage is a head effect, and head-controlled comparisons will substantially shrink claimed representation-level robustness differences between models.

one_line_idea: Robustness-intervention effects measured on small models predict their effects on foundation-scale models, enabling cheap screening before expensive integration.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The sign and approximate relative magnitude of an intervention's effect on shift robustness is preserved from small-scale to large-scale training within a model family, so a standardized small-scale screening battery predicts foundation-scale outcomes well enough to triage interventions.

one_line_idea: Background and texture shortcut reliance survives foundation-model scale essentially unchanged; scale reduces failure frequency but not the failure mechanism.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation models rely on the same shortcut features when discriminative foreground evidence weakens, so controlled foreground-background recombination tests will show the same qualitative failure pattern as older models, with only the threshold shifted.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-B-046 (texture/shortcut bias; G-065 claims scale reduces frequency but not mechanism)

one_line_idea: Retrieval and classification robustness of the same vision-language model diverge under identical shifts, so single-task robustness certification is misleading for multi-use foundation models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Different usage modes stress different properties of the representation, so a shift that leaves classification accuracy intact can severely degrade retrieval quality of the same model on the same data, and vice versa, making task-conditional robustness profiles necessary.

one_line_idea: Instruction tuning and preference alignment of vision-language assistants degrade the distribution-shift robustness of their underlying visual competence, an unmeasured robustness tax.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The narrowing of visual data during alignment stages pulls visual representations toward the instruction-data distribution, so assistant variants will show larger shifted-input degradation than their base models on matched visual tasks, with the tax growing across successive alignment stages.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Instruction tuning / preference alignment as an unmeasured robustness tax on VLM visual competence — new axis, safety-relevant.

one_line_idea: Benchmark domains are confounded bundles of style, content, and class-balance factors, and factorized shift benchmarks would reattribute much of what the field calls domain gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Decomposing existing benchmark domain gaps by controlling factors one at a time will show that class balance and content composition explain a large share of measured gaps, with pure rendering style a smaller contributor than assumed, changing which methods look effective.

one_line_idea: As in-distribution accuracy saturates, effective-robustness slopes become statistically unidentifiable, and the field needs harder in-distribution benchmarks merely to keep measuring robustness.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] With in-distribution scores compressed into a narrow range, the leverage needed to estimate robustness trends vanishes, so recent claims of above-trend robustness for frontier models are statistically fragile and sensitive to a handful of points.

one_line_idea: No robustness method Pareto-dominates across shift types, and shift-type profiles should replace single-number robustness leaderboards.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Method gains are strongly shift-type-specific with pervasive trade-offs, so across a broad method panel virtually no method will dominate another on all shift families, and averaged leaderboards mask anticorrelated specializations.

one_line_idea: Subpopulation-shift benchmarks overstate the availability of group labels, and under realistic group-label-free conditions the reported superiority of group-robust methods over plain training shrinks or vanishes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The advantage of group-robust methods is concentrated in their privileged access to group labels for model selection, so under a strict no-group-information protocol, including selection, their worst-group performance advantage over well-tuned plain training will largely disappear.

one_line_idea: Adversarially-filtered hard test sets measure disagreement with the filter model rather than distribution shift, and robustness conclusions drawn from them are filter-relative artifacts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Performance on filter-constructed sets is dominated by a model's representational similarity to the filter model rather than by robustness to any natural distribution, so scores on such sets will be predictable from model-filter similarity and will misrank models relative to unfiltered hard-case evaluation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Adversarially-filtered test sets measure disagreement with the filter model, making robustness conclusions filter-relative artifacts. Sharp, protocol-level, non-template.

one_line_idea: Caching and re-using per-condition adapters, a domain memory, beats continual gradient updating under recurring shift conditions and eliminates catastrophic forgetting by construction.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Maintaining a library of lightweight condition-specific adapter states, with unsupervised retrieval of the matching adapter per input batch, outperforms continual updating on recurring streams because retrieval replaces re-learning and isolation prevents interference.

one_line_idea: The optimal adaptation learning rate under gradual drift is a function of measurable drift speed, and an adaptive-rate law derived from it beats every fixed-rate configuration.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] There is a stable functional relationship between drift speed, estimable from windowed embedding statistics, and the regret-minimizing adaptation rate, so a controller that sets the rate from estimated speed will approach oracle-rate performance across drift regimes without per-deployment tuning.

one_line_idea: Long-horizon stability of online adaptation is governed by the dimensionality of the updated parameter subspace, and full-parameter online updating diverges with probability approaching one.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Divergence risk on unbounded unlabeled streams grows sharply with updated-subspace dimensionality at fixed step size, producing a stability-capacity frontier where low-dimensional updates are stable but expressivity-limited and full updates are expressive but almost surely divergent over long horizons.

one_line_idea: A divergence anchor to the frozen source model replaces stored source data in online adaptation, giving replay-level stability at zero storage and no privacy cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The stabilizing content of source replay is the anchoring of predictions near source behavior on non-shifted inputs, which a prediction-divergence penalty against the frozen source copy provides equivalently, so anchored adaptation will match replay-based stability across long streams without any stored data.

one_line_idea: Test-time adaptation methods silently assume covariate shift, and under label-conditional drift they confidently adapt in the wrong direction, making things worse than no adaptation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When the conditional relationship drifts, as in changed visual conventions or evolving category usage, the same objectives that help under covariate shift produce systematically harmful updates, and the harm scales with adaptation strength, creating a regime where stronger methods are strictly worse.

one_line_idea: Self-supervised test-time training helps only when the auxiliary task is statistically coupled to the shift, and a computable coupling diagnostic predicts its sign of effect.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The effect of test-time training is governed by the correlation between auxiliary-task gradients and the gradients that would reduce main-task error under the specific shift, so a coupling coefficient estimated from labeled probe shifts predicts the sign and rough size of the benefit on new shifts.

one_line_idea: Online adaptation methods are broken by realistic non-uniform arrival processes such as class bursts, and arrival-robustness should be a first-class evaluation axis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Popular adaptation methods implicitly rely on within-window class diversity, so realistic bursty arrival will cause prior-collapse updates and accuracy loss even with zero distribution shift, and method rankings under bursty arrival will differ sharply from shuffled-arrival rankings.

one_line_idea: Generic distribution-divergence measures do not predict transfer performance drop across domains, while cheap hypothesis-disagreement measures do, and the field keeps reporting the wrong quantity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Task-agnostic divergences correlate weakly with realized accuracy drop because they weight task-irrelevant variation, whereas disagreement between hypotheses trained or probed on the two domains tracks the drop closely, making disagreement the correct reportable statistic.

one_line_idea: Classical domain-adaptation generalization bounds are numerically vacuous at foundation scale yet ordinally predictive, and quantifying this rescues theory as a ranking tool.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Although the bound values are vacuous, their variation across domain pairs and models preserves ordering information, so bound-derived quantities rank transfer difficulty and method suitability nearly as well as expensive empirical trials, making theory useful ordinally where it fails numerically.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Anti-debunk: theory bounds are numerically vacuous yet ordinally predictive — rescues theory as a ranking tool. Genre-diversifying; Judge B folded it into G-087, this judge protects it (divergence recorded).

one_line_idea: Most accuracy degradation of foundation models under natural shift is captured by a two-parameter description, class-prior change plus uniform margin erosion, enabling label-free degradation forecasting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For strong pretrained models, natural shifts act on the output geometry primarily through a shift in effective class priors and a roughly uniform shrinkage of logit margins, so a two-parameter model fit on a small labeled probe predicts full-benchmark degradation curves and per-class error redistribution.

one_line_idea: Enforcing invariance to a nuisance factor provably trades away robustness to shifts correlated with that factor, and the tradeoff is measurable and large in controlled vision experiments.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When a deployment shift changes the relationship between a nuisance factor and labels, models trained invariant to that factor degrade more than non-invariant models, producing a quantifiable invariance-robustness frontier rather than a free lunch.

one_line_idea: Importance weighting for covariate shift, long dismissed as hopeless in high dimensions, becomes practical when density ratios are estimated in foundation-model embedding space.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation embeddings compress shift-relevant variation into low effective dimension where density ratios are estimable with controlled variance, so embedding-space importance weighting delivers reliable covariate-shift correction for reweighting evaluation and fine-tuning, reviving a method the field wrote off.

one_line_idea: Language is an adaptation surface: systematic per-domain prompt construction matches gradient-based adaptation of vision-language models at a tiny fraction of the cost and risk.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a broad class of deployment shifts, the accuracy recoverable by any unsupervised adaptation is largely recoverable by domain-conditioned prompt construction alone, generated by a fixed systematic procedure from a short domain characterization, because the text tower already encodes the needed domain priors.

one_line_idea: The text tower has its own distribution-shift problem: class-name register, dialect, and terminology shifts degrade vision-language classification as much as image shifts, and no benchmark measures this axis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Semantically equivalent but lexically shifted class vocabularies induce accuracy drops comparable in magnitude to standard image shifts, with the damage concentrated in classes whose common names diverge from web-caption conventions, constituting an unmeasured second axis of shift.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-052 (name/synonym sensitivity family; G-096 widens it to a text-tower shift axis)
judge_c.anomaly_note: The text tower has its own distribution-shift problem (register, dialect, terminology) as large as image shift and unmeasured — genuinely new benchmark axis.

one_line_idea: Under image distribution shift, vision-language assistants lean harder on language priors, so their accuracy degrades gracefully while their visual grounding collapses, and accuracy-only evaluation hides the swap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] As image quality or distribution degrades, these systems substitute language-prior guessing for visual evidence, so measured accuracy declines slowly while grounding metrics, such as consistency with image-specific perturbations, decline steeply, meaning robustness claims based on accuracy measure prior strength rather than perception.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-C-089 (language-prior hallucination; G-097 is the under-shift grounding-collapse variant)
judge_c.anomaly_note: Accuracy degrades gracefully while grounding collapses: language priors silently replace vision under shift. Distinct hidden-failure-swap mechanism.

one_line_idea: The caption-style provenance of pretraining data determines which visual shifts a vision-language model is robust to, giving each model a predictable robustness fingerprint.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Caption provenance controls which visual variations pretraining associates with stable semantics, so models trained with different caption styles will exhibit systematically different per-shift-family robustness profiles, predictable from measurable properties of their caption distributions.

one_line_idea: Cross-modal agreement between image and text pathways is a label-free estimator of shift harm specific to vision-language models, outperforming confidence-based estimators.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Degradation of the visual pathway under shift breaks its agreement with text-side expectations in measurable ways, so agreement statistics between image embeddings and text-anchored structure estimate accuracy loss more reliably than confidence-based methods, because the text side provides a shift-stable reference.

one_line_idea: Generative vision models used as classifiers have a qualitatively different distribution-shift robustness profile than discriminative foundation models, defining an unexplored complementary paradigm.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generative classification degrades under different shift families than discriminative classification, being more stable under low-level and style shifts that preserve generability while failing differently under semantic novelty, so the two paradigms have complementary robustness profiles exploitable by simple combination.

one_line_idea: The synthetic-to-real gap in super-resolution is dominated by unmodeled noise and compression, not by blur-kernel mismatch, so blind-kernel estimation attacks a second-order problem.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Matching realistic sensor noise and compression statistics alone, while keeping a deliberately wrong bicubic kernel, recovers the majority of the synthetic-to-real transfer gap; kernel realism alone recovers only a minority share.

one_line_idea: Large randomized degradation pipelines teach models the artifact statistics of the pipeline itself, and a small set of camera-measured degradations transfers better to real photos.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on such pipelines overfit to pipeline-specific artifact combinations that rarely occur in real captures, and a compact degradation set measured from a few real camera and ISP configurations yields better real-world transfer at equal training cost.

one_line_idea: The composition order of degradations matters more than degradation diversity for real-world restoration transfer.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Holding marginal degradation distributions fixed, training with the physically correct stage order transfers substantially better to real photos than order-shuffled training, because artifact interactions are order-dependent.

one_line_idea: Per-image single-kernel estimation in blind SR is a mis-specified problem because real point-spread functions are spatially varying and chromatically aberrated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual error from forcing a single uniform kernel is larger than the error from moderate kernel misestimation, so improving per-image kernel estimators has hit a floor imposed by the uniformity assumption itself.

one_line_idea: Modeling degradations in the raw sensor domain and passing them through an ISP simulator transfers better than modeling degradations directly in sRGB space.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Degradations synthesized in raw and rendered through an ISP model reproduce the correlated, signal-dependent artifact structure of real photos better than sRGB-domain synthesis, yielding stronger real-world restoration transfer.

one_line_idea: Degradation pipelines undersample the mild-degradation regime that dominates real photos, so blind models are miscalibrated toward over-restoration of nearly clean inputs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The mismatch between the training severity distribution and the deployment severity distribution causes systematic over-sharpening and hallucination on mildly degraded inputs, and reweighting training severity toward the deployment distribution fixes it without hurting hard cases much.

one_line_idea: Modern phone photos are already processed by on-device neural enhancement, so the dominant real-world degradation family is neural-network-induced, and classic degradation models are increasingly obsolete.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual degradations in modern phone photos are dominated by artifacts of on-device neural processing (over-smoothing, texture invention, fusion ghosting) that classic blur-noise-compression pipelines do not model, causing restoration models to misfire on the newest devices.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Era claim: dominant real-world degradations are now neural-network-induced (on-device enhancement), making classic degradation models obsolete. Field-redefining if true.

one_line_idea: Many practically low-quality images were never downsampled, so framing super-resolution as inverse downsampling is a category error for a large share of use cases.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For natively low-detail images, models trained as downsampling inverters produce characteristic failure modes (wrong detail scale, gridded texture) that a detail-synthesis formulation without a downsampling assumption avoids.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Category-error claim: much low-quality imagery was never downsampled, so SR-as-inverse-downsampling is the wrong problem statement for a large share of use.

one_line_idea: Blind-SR kernel estimates are echoes of the learned image prior rather than measurements, and they collapse on images that violate natural-image statistics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Kernel estimators primarily report the kernel that reconciles the input with the natural-image prior, so on non-natural content (synthetic patterns, text, star fields) their estimates become systematically wrong in predictable directions.

one_line_idea: A degradation-space distance between training pipeline outputs and real photos predicts real-world transfer better than benchmark scores do.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A distributional distance computed in a space of artifact statistics (noise spectra, edge profiles, block-artifact features) between pipeline-degraded images and a target real corpus predicts a model's real-world performance better than its synthetic benchmark score.

one_line_idea: Real-world paired SR benchmarks reward slight blur because zoom-lens pair alignment errors make hedged, soft predictions optimal under full-reference metrics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual misalignment in paired real-world benchmarks makes slightly blurred predictions score better than sharp, correctly restored ones, so leaderboard optimization on these datasets systematically selects for blur.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Benchmark-incentive mechanism (alignment error rewards hedged blur) that explains a known aesthetic pathology; absorbs H-027.

one_line_idea: Unpaired real-world restoration methods secretly depend on the same hand-crafted degradation assumptions they claim to avoid.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The degradation generators inside unpaired methods are constrained (architecture, losses, cycle constraints) in ways that encode nearly the same blur-noise-compression family as hand-crafted pipelines, so they fail on degradation types outside that family just like synthetic training does.

one_line_idea: Per-image test-time adaptation from internal recurrence beats adding more pretraining data for real-world restoration at foundation scale.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For real photos with atypical degradations, briefly adapting a large pretrained restoration model to the test image's internal statistics yields larger quality gains than scaling the pretraining set by an order of magnitude.

one_line_idea: Blind restoration fails as a cliff, not a slope, just outside its training severity range, and the cliff location is predictable from training data alone.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model quality degrades gracefully within the training severity envelope but collapses abruptly just beyond it, and the collapse point can be predicted from the training distribution without running the model on extreme inputs.

one_line_idea: A small mixture-of-experts routed by degradation archetype beats a monolithic blind model of equal total capacity on real photos.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Marginalizing over degradation archetypes in one network forces averaged inverse operators; explicit routing to archetype experts removes this averaging penalty and wins at matched total parameters and training compute.

one_line_idea: A single user-facing fidelity-versus-enhancement dial captures most practical value of degradation estimation, making precise automatic estimation unnecessary for consumer restoration.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Human users given one scalar control over restoration aggressiveness reach output quality within a small margin of oracle degradation-aware restoration, so the practical value of automatic degradation estimation is far lower than its research prominence suggests.

one_line_idea: The blind restoration setting ignores freely available capture metadata that carries most of the degradation information the models struggle to estimate.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Conditioning restoration on standard capture metadata recovers a large fraction of the gap between blind and oracle-degradation restoration, at zero estimation cost.

one_line_idea: Restoration models fail systematically on non-photographic content because both degradation models and image priors are photo-centric, and a content-type failure taxonomy would expose this blind spot.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On non-photographic content, restoration models exhibit reproducible failure families (halo artifacts on flat-color edges, texture invention on smooth fills, font distortion) whose severity is predictable from the content type, and light content-type conditioning removes most of these failures.

one_line_idea: Analog degradations in old photos form a structurally different family from digital ones, and models trained on digital pipelines hallucinate when facing film-era artifacts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Digital-pipeline-trained models misinterpret analog artifacts as content or as digital noise, producing characteristic hallucinations, and explicit analog degradation synthesis (grain models, scratch simulation, halftone patterns) fixes most failures without any architecture change.

one_line_idea: The practically relevant perception-distortion tradeoff is per-region, not per-model, and a single global operating point is wrong for most images.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Human preference is maximized by spatially varying the tradeoff (high fidelity on faces and text, high perceptual quality on stochastic textures), and a spatially adaptive model beats every fixed-tradeoff model on overall preference.

one_line_idea: Learned perceptual metrics are gameable by artifact styles matched to their training distribution, and metric-tuned SR models exhibit a recognizable metric texture.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Optimizing restoration outputs against learned metrics produces a systematic, classifiable texture signature that scores well under the metric while diverging from natural image statistics, and human raters can learn to spot it.

one_line_idea: Human preference between faithful and hallucinated restorations reverses with viewing time and ground-truth knowledge, so time-limited studies structurally favor hallucination.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Preference for sharp hallucinated outputs at short exposures flips toward fidelity-preserving outputs under extended inspection, zoom access, or when raters know the true content, meaning current protocols encode a hallucination bias into the field's optimization target.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Psychophysics: preference between faithful and hallucinated restorations reverses with viewing time and ground-truth knowledge — time-limited studies structurally favor hallucination.

one_line_idea: The empirical perception-distortion frontier is largely a loss mis-specification artifact, and a properly specified conditional likelihood model can dominate both endpoints simultaneously.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Much of the practically observed tradeoff arises from mis-specified losses (pixel regression versus adversarial mixtures) rather than from the information-theoretic limit, so models trained with better-specified posterior objectives can improve perception and distortion together relative to today's frontier.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Attacks the perception-distortion frontier itself as a loss mis-specification artifact, claiming a properly specified conditional likelihood dominates both endpoints. High-risk high-reward contrarian.

one_line_idea: Replacing distortion-to-reference with consistency-to-observation as the fidelity axis makes the perception tradeoff much milder, and consistency should be the reported fidelity metric for generative restoration.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Perceptual quality conflicts strongly with single-reference distortion but only weakly with observation consistency, so reframing fidelity as data consistency reveals that high realism and high fidelity-to-evidence are jointly achievable.

one_line_idea: Human-preferred restorations systematically degrade machine consumption (OCR, recognition), so perceptual quality and machine quality are diverging objectives needing separate outputs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Perceptually tuned restoration alters or destroys machine-relevant evidence (glyph shapes, fine boundaries, texture statistics) such that recognition systems perform worse on human-preferred restorations than on distortion-optimized ones of the same inputs.

one_line_idea: Restoration models should output a hallucination map, and cross-seed variance of generative restorers already provides one that flags fabricated regions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-pixel dispersion across sampling seeds is a usable hallucination indicator: regions with high cross-seed variance are dominated by prior invention, and exposing this map materially changes user trust decisions.

one_line_idea: Perceived restoration quality saturates under realistic viewing conditions, and beyond a resolvable-detail threshold the field is optimizing differences invisible to users.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under representative viewing conditions, preference differences between recent top restoration models vanish for a large fraction of images, meaning reported improvements increasingly live below the visibility threshold.

one_line_idea: GAN-versus-diffusion differences in restoration quality are dominated by training data and loss weighting rather than the generative framework itself.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under matched backbone, data, and compute, adversarial and diffusion restoration reach statistically comparable perceptual quality, and the perceived diffusion advantage mostly reflects confounded comparisons.

one_line_idea: Hallucination severity in generative SR scales with prior strength: the better the generative model, the more confidently it fabricates the wrong content.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] As the prior improves (more data, larger models), fabricated content becomes simultaneously more plausible and less faithful in evidence-poor regions, so semantic hallucination rate on ambiguous inputs increases with prior quality rather than decreasing.

one_line_idea: Face restoration homogenizes identity, drifting restored faces toward the training distribution's typical attributes, measurable as systematic embedding shift.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Restored faces exhibit a consistent drift in identity-embedding space toward dense regions of the training distribution, so restoration reduces inter-identity variance and biases perceived attributes toward the training majority.

one_line_idea: Restoration models should abstain on illegible text instead of fabricating legible wrong characters, and text-aware abstention is implementable without hurting non-text quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A text-region-aware restoration policy that preserves illegibility (or marks uncertainty) when character evidence is insufficient eliminates most harmful text hallucination at negligible cost to overall perceptual quality.

one_line_idea: Late-stage sampling in diffusion-based SR is only weakly conditioned on the input, so the fine detail users see is mostly prior draw rather than evidence.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dependence of the output on the degraded input is concentrated in early, coarse-structure sampling stages, while late stages that synthesize fine texture are close to unconditional, meaning the visible detail is largely input-independent.

one_line_idea: Sample diversity in stochastic restoration is misallocated: seeds vary irrelevant texture while collapsing on semantically ambiguous content where diversity actually matters.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-seed variation concentrates in perceptually irrelevant micro-texture while semantically ambiguous regions (which face, which character) collapse to a single mode, so the advertised diversity does not represent the true posterior where it counts.

one_line_idea: Fixed default guidance scales in diffusion restoration are wrong for most images, and per-image guidance calibration from consistency residuals recovers substantial quality for free.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The optimal guidance scale varies widely per image with degradation severity and content, and a cheap automatic calibrator that picks the scale by minimizing re-degradation residual plus a realism proxy beats any fixed scale on average.

one_line_idea: Cross-seed agreement in generative restoration is treated as certainty, but agreement can be confidently wrong, and the agreement-accuracy relationship has never been calibrated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Conditional mode collapse makes seed agreement a miscalibrated certainty signal: a measurable fraction of high-agreement regions are systematically wrong, and the agreement-accuracy curve deviates far from the ideal.

one_line_idea: Generative restorers are unstable inverse maps: imperceptible input perturbations flip hallucinated semantic content, undermining forensic use.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Tiny, imperceptible perturbations of a degraded input can deterministically switch semantically meaningful restored content (different characters, different facial features), demonstrating that restored semantics are functions of noise-level input details no honest analyst would consider informative.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Generative restorers as unstable inverse maps: imperceptible input perturbations flip hallucinated semantic content — forensic-grade failure, non-template.

one_line_idea: Generative restorers can inject memorized training images into outputs on ambiguous inputs, and restoration needs a memorization-probe protocol like generation has.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When observation evidence is weak, restoration models sometimes complete inputs with near-copies of specific training images (faces, artworks, scenes), constituting a privacy and copyright hazard that current evaluation never surfaces.

one_line_idea: The field needs a formal restoration-versus-reimagination boundary based on information recoverable from the observation, and most perceptual SR crosses it without disclosure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] An operational criterion comparing observation-derived information against prior-injected information per region can classify outputs into restoration and reimagination regimes, and applying it will show that popular perceptual SR operates mostly in the reimagination regime at high magnification factors.

one_line_idea: Text-to-image foundation priors import aesthetic bias into restoration: outputs drift toward beautified renditions rather than faithful ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation-prior restorers systematically shift outputs toward higher saturation, cleaner skin, tidier scenes, and removal of mundane imperfections relative to ground truth, a measurable aesthetic drift absent in task-trained restorers.

one_line_idea: Vision-language-guided restoration converts caption errors into confident pixel hallucinations, a compounding error mode absent from caption-free restorers.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When the captioner misreads degraded content, the restoration inherits and amplifies the error, rendering the wrong semantics with high visual confidence, so caption guidance is net-harmful on exactly the ambiguous inputs it was meant to help.

one_line_idea: Restoration quality saturates with model scale much earlier than generation quality because the task is observation-bounded, making restoration a poor showcase for foundation-scale compute.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because restoration outputs are constrained by observation information, quality gains from scale saturate quickly once the prior suffices to fill the posterior, so scale ladders in restoration show early plateaus on fidelity metrics even as generation metrics keep improving.

one_line_idea: Universal all-in-one restoration models suffer negative transfer on hard cases, losing to per-task specialists at matched capacity despite average-metric parity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Multi-task restoration training induces negative transfer concentrated in the hardest quantiles of each task, so all-in-one models match specialists on averages while losing clearly on per-task tail performance, which averages hide.

one_line_idea: Self-supervised foundation features are worse perceptual-loss backbones than older supervised features because SSL objectives explicitly learn invariances that a fidelity metric must not have.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Augmentation-invariance training makes SSL features blind to exactly the shifts, recolorings, and local deformations that restoration losses must penalize, so SSL-feature losses train models with more geometric and color drift than classification-feature losses.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Mechanism inversion: SSL invariances are exactly what a fidelity metric must not have, so SSL features make WORSE perceptual losses than older supervised features.

one_line_idea: Instruction-based restoration is prompt-fragile: paraphrases of the same enhancement request produce materially different outputs, and no benchmark measures this instability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Output quality and character vary substantially across semantically equivalent phrasings of the same restoration request, so reported results are prompt-tuned upper bounds and real-user experience is systematically worse and inconsistent.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-B-026 / W13-P1-C-020 (prompt-jitter/paraphrase sensitivity family ported to instruction restoration; kept because the fragility-as-flaw claim and substrate are new)

one_line_idea: In-context restoration examples act as style anchors rather than degradation evidence: shuffled or mismatched example pairs work nearly as well as correct ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models mostly ignore the degradation relationship inside example pairs and use them as output-style references, so deliberately mismatched examples (wrong degradation, unrelated content) reduce performance far less than the in-context framing predicts.

judge_c.anomaly_note: In-context restoration examples act as style anchors, not degradation evidence — shuffled examples work; attribution claim about an interface everyone trusts.

one_line_idea: Repeated passes through neural processing (restoration, editing, recompression) create a compounding neural degradation family that classic degradation models cannot express, and future restorers must model it explicitly.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Iterated neural processing produces distinctive compounding artifacts (statistics drift, over-regularized texture, semantic residue from earlier edits) that classic pipelines never synthesize, and restorers trained with simulated neural-processing chains will beat classic-pipeline models on such content.

one_line_idea: Standard SR ground truths are themselves degraded, imposing a hidden quality ceiling and penalizing models that exceed ground-truth quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable fraction of reference images in standard benchmarks contains visible degradations, and models producing cleaner-than-reference outputs are systematically penalized by full-reference metrics, distorting method rankings near the quality ceiling.

one_line_idea: Luma-only PSNR evaluation lets SR models neglect chroma, and hidden color artifacts are widespread but unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models tuned under luma-only evaluation systematically underperform on chroma reconstruction (color bleeding, desaturation of fine structure, hue shifts at edges), and full-color evaluation would reorder methods and expose a neglected error family.

one_line_idea: No-reference quality metrics actively reward hallucination in generative SR because modern fabrication artifacts lie outside their training distortion domains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Since fabricated detail is sharp and natural-looking locally, no-reference metrics score hallucinated outputs above faithful ones, so optimizing or ranking by these metrics selects for confident fabrication.

one_line_idea: Crop-based human studies over-sample regions where hallucination looks good, and whole-image task-driven protocols would flip some perceptual-SR conclusions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Crop selection biases studies toward stochastic-texture regions where fabricated detail wins, while whole-image viewing and task-driven judgments (would you trust or share this photo) weight semantic fidelity higher and would reverse some published preferences.

one_line_idea: Expected-distortion evaluation of stochastic restorers penalizes legitimate posterior diversity, and set-based or distributional fidelity metrics are required to compare generative restoration fairly.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Single-sample-versus-single-reference scoring systematically misranks stochastic methods (penalizing honest diversity, rewarding mode-averaged blur or collapse), and set-level protocols (best-of-k, coverage-precision over samples, distributional distance to a reference set) change conclusions about which generative restorer is better.

one_line_idea: Training restoration losses in gamma-encoded sRGB misweights shadow and highlight errors, and linear-light loss computation changes model behavior visibly in low light.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Gamma-space losses over-weight shadow errors and under-weight highlight errors relative to physical error, biasing models toward shadow smoothing and highlight neglect, and computing losses in approximately linearized space yields visibly different, tonally better-balanced restorations.

one_line_idea: The field optimizes 4x magnification while deployment overwhelmingly needs mild continuous scales, and mild-scale performance is not predicted by 4x benchmark scores.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model quality at mild continuous scales correlates weakly with 4x benchmark scores because mild-scale quality is dominated by resampling finesse and identity preservation rather than by texture synthesis, so the community's flagship metric does not measure the practically dominant regime.

one_line_idea: High-resolution training targets contain sensor noise that models learn to reproduce, so part of learned texture synthesis is actually noise imitation, and denoised-target training changes the perceptual character of outputs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable component of what perceptual SR models render as fine texture is learned reproduction of target noise statistics, and training against carefully denoised targets yields models whose outputs look different in texture character while scoring similarly on structure.

one_line_idea: Real degradations vary strongly across the frame, and globally-conditioned restoration produces spatially inconsistent quality that per-region degradation conditioning fixes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On real photos, spatial degradation variance is large enough that global conditioning leaves corner regions under-restored and center regions over-restored (or vice versa), and spatially-varying degradation estimation with per-region conditioning yields consistent quality across the frame.

one_line_idea: Restoration models exploit the correlation between content and degradation in real data as a shortcut, and they misrestore counterfactual images where the correlation is broken.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models learn content-conditioned degradation expectations (denoise night scenes hard, sharpen distant subjects) and apply them even when actual degradation contradicts the content prior, producing systematic errors on counterfactual inputs like clean night photos or noisy daylight photos.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Restorers exploit content-degradation correlation as a shortcut and misrestore counterfactual images — a causal-confound claim unique in the shard.

one_line_idea: Tiled inference silently degrades large-image restoration through seam artifacts and context truncation, and patch-benchmark scores hide a whole-image quality gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Tiling introduces measurable quality loss (blending softness at seams, inconsistent hallucination across tiles, loss of global context for degradation estimation) that patch benchmarks never register, so deployed quality is systematically below benchmarked quality in a size-dependent way.

one_line_idea: Training against a single ground-truth realization teaches models false confidence at high magnification, and the one-target assumption is the root of both blur (regression) and overconfident fabrication (generation).
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The single-target convention is the common cause of the field's two signature pathologies: pixel losses average over the unacknowledged posterior (blur), and adversarial or diffusion losses pick one mode and present it as the answer (overconfident fabrication); training objectives that explicitly acknowledge target multiplicity (multi-target supervision where obtainable, posterior-aware losses) reduce both pathologies simultaneously.

one_line_idea: Eight-bit quantization of training pairs imposes an ignored information floor, causing banding-related failure modes and capping low-contrast detail recovery that higher-bit-depth training would unlock.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Quantization noise and banding in 8-bit training data teach models to reproduce or amplify banding in smooth gradients and to ignore sub-quantization-level structure, and training on higher-bit-depth pairs measurably improves smooth-gradient rendering and low-contrast texture recovery.

one_line_idea: Restored images are almost always re-compressed downstream, and optimizing restoration jointly with expected re-compression changes what the optimal output looks like, devaluing fragile hallucinated texture.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] High-frequency synthesized texture is disproportionately destroyed or distorted by downstream compression, so compression-aware restoration (optimizing quality after expected re-compression) selects different, more compression-robust outputs and beats standard models in end-to-end perceived quality after platform processing.

one_line_idea: Restoration models entangle tone and color enhancement with structural restoration, and disentangling shows part of perceived restoration quality is uncredited color grading.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable share of human preference for outputs of modern restorers is attributable to incidental tone and color changes rather than structural recovery, and factoring outputs into color transform plus structural change reveals models differ far less structurally than leaderboards suggest.

one_line_idea: Warped-frame temporal consistency metrics reward temporally stable hallucination over faithful but variable detail, making them anti-fidelity in exactly the hard cases.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] These metrics assign better scores to a model that hallucinates the same wrong detail consistently than to one that renders correct detail with slight temporal variation, so optimizing them steers video restorers toward stable fabrication.

one_line_idea: The multi-frame advantage of video SR collapses on properly anti-aliased or heavily compressed footage, because models exploit temporal aliasing as their main cross-frame cue.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Much of the measured multi-frame gain comes from aliasing patterns that shift predictably with motion; on anti-aliased or codec-smoothed footage, the recoverable cross-frame signal shrinks and video SR degrades toward per-frame SR quality.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Multi-frame video SR advantage collapses on properly anti-aliased/compressed footage because temporal aliasing is the main cross-frame cue — mechanism discovery with deployment consequences.

one_line_idea: Codec-informed video restoration using bitstream metadata (block boundaries, motion vectors, quantization levels) beats blind pixel-space restoration at equal capacity, and discarding the bitstream is an unforced error.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Codec artifacts are deterministic functions of encoding decisions recoverable from the bitstream, so conditioning restoration on bitstream metadata resolves artifact-versus-content ambiguity that pixel-only models must guess, yielding consistent quality gains especially at low bitrates.

one_line_idea: Recurrent video restorers accumulate hallucination drift over long sequences, diverging from input content in ways short-clip benchmarks never measure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Propagated state accretes synthesized detail that recursively conditions later frames, so over hundreds of frames outputs drift measurably away from evidence (texture lock-in, progressive stylization), a failure invisible at benchmark clip lengths.

one_line_idea: Short-clip training gives recurrent video restorers an implicit state-reset bias, making their effective temporal receptive field far shorter than architecture diagrams claim.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training on short clips teaches the recurrence to discount information beyond the training-clip horizon, so the effective temporal receptive field saturates near the training length and additional context frames at inference contribute nearly nothing.

one_line_idea: Face-video enhancement alters lip and expression micro-motion, measurably changing perceived speech and emotion, a safety-relevant failure invisible to every current metric.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generative video enhancement modifies mouth shapes and micro-expressions enough to change lip-reading interpretation and perceived affect in a measurable fraction of clips, meaning enhancement can alter the communicative record while passing all quality metrics.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Face-video enhancement alters lip/expression micro-motion, changing perceived speech and emotion — safety-relevant, invisible to every current metric.

one_line_idea: Video restoration allocates compute suboptimally across frames: temporal information saturates after a few neighbors, and reallocating compute to per-frame quality dominates at fixed budget.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The marginal value of additional context frames decays fast (most recoverable cross-frame information lives in the nearest few frames), so at a fixed FLOP budget, small-window models with stronger per-frame processing beat wide-window models with thinner processing.

one_line_idea: Synthetic video SR benchmarks miss the coupling between motion blur, shutter time, and frame rate in real capture, and this coupling breaks synthetic-to-real transfer more than spatial degradation mismatch.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on spatially-degraded-but-temporally-sharp frames misinterpret real motion blur as spatial blur, applying wrong corrections along motion trajectories, and adding physically coupled temporal blur synthesis to training closes more of the real-video gap than improving spatial degradation realism.

one_line_idea: Restore-then-recognize pipelines lose to recognition models trained directly on degraded inputs, because restoration destroys machine-relevant evidence while adding human-pleasing detail.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Restoration is a lossy, prior-injecting transform of the evidence; degradation-adapted recognition preserves task-relevant information better, so restore-then-recognize underperforms degraded-input fine-tuning at matched effort across common tasks and severities.

flags: wave1_adjacent:W13-P1-D-030 (restoration-for-machines tension: SR preprocessing biases detection)

one_line_idea: Generative restoration invalidates images as evidence, and restoration systems for forensic contexts should emit per-region fidelity certificates grounded in observation consistency.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A certification layer that decomposes each output region into evidence-supported and prior-injected components, with quantified consistency bounds under the estimated forward model, can be attached to restoration outputs and would change downstream trust decisions in measurable ways.

one_line_idea: Natural-photo priors contaminate scientific imagery: restoration models trained on photographs inject natural-image statistics into scientific data, creating plausible artifacts that could mislead analysis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Photo-trained restorers systematically reshape scientific image content toward natural-image statistics (edge sharpening, texture regularization, structure completion), producing artifacts that domain experts judge plausible but that alter quantitative measurements derived from the images.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Natural-photo priors contaminate scientific imagery with plausible artifacts — hard-domain coupling claim; protect for the underserved-domains agenda.

one_line_idea: Restoration-as-decoder compression schemes (send low quality, restore at receiver) are evaluated with perceptual metrics that hide semantic drift, and round-trip semantic audits would cap their claimed bitrate savings.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At the advertised low bitrates, decoder-side generation alters semantic content (object identity details, text, counts) at rates that perceptual and distributional metrics do not register, and a semantic round-trip audit (does the reconstruction preserve task-relevant facts) would show the effective safe bitrate is substantially higher than claimed.

one_line_idea: For machine consumption, restoring feature embeddings directly beats restoring pixels first: pixel space is a human-oriented bottleneck that wastes capacity on visually pleasing but task-irrelevant detail.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Learning a degraded-to-clean mapping directly in the feature space of the downstream model preserves task information better and costs less than pixel restoration, because pixel realism constraints are irrelevant to the consumer and actively divert capacity.
